name: WordPress
description: The blogging and website platform, with its own MariaDB server beside it. The database is reachable only from WordPress, on a private network with nothing published.

access.note: WordPress has no administrator until someone makes one: the first visitor to https://<domain>/wp-admin/install.php chooses the site title, the administrator's name and password, and becomes its owner — open it the moment the deployment is ready rather than leaving it unclaimed. The database password is generated here and only WordPress and MariaDB are given it.

secrets.name: db-password
secrets.label: Database password
secrets.description: WordPress signs in to MariaDB with this. Generated here and given to both services.

secrets.name: db-root-password
secrets.label: MariaDB root password
secrets.description: For administering the database by hand; WordPress never uses it.

services.name: wordpress
services.purpose: The site and its admin, behind the domain

volumes.name: site
volumes.purpose: WordPress itself, its configuration, themes, plugins and uploads

services.name: db
services.purpose: MariaDB, holding every post, page, user and setting

automation.name: Nightly backup
automation.description: Archives the site and database volumes every night.

update.notes: WordPress updates its own files from wp-admin; the image tag only decides the copy a fresh volume starts from. MariaDB moves between major versions with mariadb-upgrade, which the image runs on start when MARIADB_AUTO_UPGRADE is set; take a backup first.
